one_line_contribution: That the memory injection budget k is simultaneously a variance lever and therefore a selection-bias lever: the fraction of a reflective prompt optimizer's reported validation gain that is pure winner's-curse artefact is larger at k=7 than k=0, measured with a null-proposal optimizer paired by optimizer seed, plus a measurement of whether common random numbers (item-sharing vs seed-sharing) survive in an interactive agent. I can state it, but the first half is close to a corollary of things the proposal itself already assumes.
closest_prior_work: Three threats, in decreasing order. (1) Dodge et al. 2019 'Show Your Work', which the proposal correctly disclaims for the mechanism — but the disclaimer does more damage than acknowledged: given max-of-N inflation ~ sigma*sqrt(2 ln N) (which the proposal itself adopts in P7), P2 follows arithmetically from P1 plus a fixed N. If more injected context raises sigma, larger selection bias is entailed, not discovered; E1's 76,800 rollouts are then a calibration of a known formula, not a test of a new claim. (2) On the remedy side, Shi et al., 'Efficient Prompt Optimization Through the Lens of Best Arm Identification' (TRIPLE, NeurIPS 2024) frames prompt selection under a fixed evaluation budget explicitly as noisy best-arm identification and is a much closer neighbour to E2b than ProTeGi's UCB; it is not cited and not run as a baseline. (3) For P1, prompt/context-sensitivity work (Sclar et al., FormatSpread, ICLR 2024) and the long-context degradation literature ('lost in the middle' and its 2025 successors) already establish that added context moves accuracy and its dispersion; 'injecting 7 items raises run-to-run sigma by >=1.3x' will read to many reviewers as instrumentation of an expected effect. The track's own prior null replicate is correctly identified as colliding with P6 and correctly demoted.
strongest_objection: The headline claim is tested at n=4, with a power assumption that contradicts the hypothesis being tested. P2's primary endpoint is a within-seed paired contrast of run-level null gain across k=0 and k=7 with exactly 4 optimizer seeds (3 df), and the stated MDE of ~2.8 points depends on a *guessed* between-run SD of 1.5 points. But run-level null gain is itself a max-of-N extreme statistic whose between-run dispersion scales with the very sigma the proposal predicts is inflated at k=7 — so under H1 the k=7 arm has the larger between-run SD by construction, the paired differences are heteroscedastic, and the design is least powered exactly where it needs precision. The proposal's own escape hatch ("if between-run SD exceeds 2.2 we report P2 as directional") concedes the likeliest outcome: the primary claim is unresolvable and the paper falls back to E2, which the risk section itself calls the part most exposed to being scooped. Compounding this, the derived endpoint 'curse fraction = null gain / real gain' with a threshold of 0.15 absolute has a denominator that this track's own prior work suggests may be near zero on a 7B agent (optimizer gain was redistribution, not accuracy); a ratio with a near-zero, noisy denominator across 4 seeds is not an estimable quantity, and no rule is given for what happens when real gain is <=0 in some seeds.
what_would_fix_it: Re-budget E1 rather than add compute: cut generations from 8 to 5 and candidates from 12 to 8 (1,600 rollouts/run) and spend the savings on 8-10 optimizer seeds per cell, so the primary paired contrast has usable df and the between-run SD is estimated rather than assumed; N is a controlled variable in P7 anyway, so a smaller N costs a design point, not a claim. Make null gain in accuracy points the sole primary endpoint and demote curse fraction to a descriptive ratio reported only when real gain exceeds the null-replicate floor. Add the accuracy-matched control described under missing_baseline so the k-contrast is not confounded with headroom. State the decoding temperature and include a greedy-vs-sampled arm in E0 — if evaluation is near-greedy, the decoding variance component and the whole seed-sharing half of P3 are degenerate by construction. Build the E2 tensor from candidates harvested at both k=0 and k=7 (10 each) so selection-rule conclusions can be stated as a function of the injection budget rather than only inside the noisy arm. Finally, drop P5 from the novelty list: that a common shrinkage factor applied to deviations from a common mean preserves ranks under equal allocation is an algebraic identity, not a finding; keep it as a one-paragraph remark and let the empirical part be the unequal-allocation case.
missing_baseline: An accuracy- and length-matched k=0 control. At k=7 the seed prompt is known (from this track's own prior result) to score *worse* than at k=0, so a larger null-optimizer gain at k=7 is fully explained by more headroom, regression toward the mean on a bounded binary metric, and lower baseline accuracy sitting nearer the steep part of the binomial variance curve p(1-p) — none of which require 'memory inflates selection bias'. The plan has no arm that holds baseline accuracy fixed while varying k, so P2's contrast cannot distinguish its own mechanism from a floor effect. Two cheap controls fix this: (i) a k=0 arm with a deliberately weakened seed prompt matched to the k=7 baseline accuracy; (ii) a k=7-token-matched arm injecting irrelevant or shuffled bank items, which holds context length and episode length fixed while removing retrieved-experience content, separating 'volume as tokens' from 'volume as memory'. Secondary omissions: no best-arm-identification/TRIPLE-style baseline in E2b, and no k=0 outcome tensor in E2.
preprint_collision: This is the weakest section and, by the standard that an unsearched novelty claim is a weakness rather than a neutral, it materially lowers my scores. The check reports *zero* successful searches — every query errored — and self-labels 'novelty unverified, for the second consecutive round.' The honesty is real and I credit the refusal to fabricate citations, but a submission arriving twice with no retrieved literature has not established novelty, and the section's own text identifies the highest-risk niche (2025-2026 preprints on agent evaluation noise floors, benchmark reproducibility audits, and winner's-curse corrections for prompt optimizers) as active and plausible for a collision. I cannot name a specific 2026 preprint from here, but the named risks are concrete: best-arm-identification/fixed-budget selection for prompt optimization is an existing published line (TRIPLE, NeurIPS 2024) that the section does not mention at all, and inference-nondeterminism / eval-noise-floor reporting for LLM agents is a heavily populated 2025-2026 area. Separately, the pre-registered kill-switch is set so narrowly as to be near-vacuous: the project is killed only if a single paper reports *both* the k-interaction *and* the CRN item/seed decomposition for interactive agents. Almost no preprint will satisfy that conjunction, so the clause functions as insurance rather than as a commitment; a per-claim demotion rule (as already written for the P1/P2 case) should be the operative standard, and the search log must land before compute is spent, not alongside it.
